title: Synthesis: miután, mielőtt, and Multi-Subject Narration

sections.content: This lesson doesn't teach new grammar: it combines everything from this unit — *miután*/*mielőtt* subordinate clauses and multi-subject narration with named and collective subjects — into the kind of fluent, connected answer you'd actually give in a naturalization interview to a question like: "Mesélje el, hogyan foglalták el a magyarok a Kárpát-medencét!" ("Tell me how the Magyars occupied the Carpathian Basin.")

items.spanish: Miután a besenyők nyomása kiszorította őket Etelközből, a magyar törzsek nyugat felé indultak, és a Kárpátok hágóin át érkeztek az új hazába.
items.english: After Pecheneg pressure pushed them out of Etelköz, the Magyar tribes set out westward and arrived in the new homeland through the passes of the Carpathians.

items.spanish: A hét törzs vezetői vérszerződéssel egyesültek, mielőtt Árpád fejedelem bevezette őket a medencébe.
items.english: The leaders of the seven tribes united by a blood oath, before Prince Árpád led them into the basin.

items.spanish: Miután a magyarok 907-ben megvédték új hazájukat a pozsonyi csatában, a honfoglalás emléke fontos része maradt a magyar nemzeti identitásnak.
items.english: After the Magyars defended their new homeland at the Battle of Pozsony in 907, the memory of the honfoglalás has remained an important part of Hungarian national identity.

sections.content: A strong summary answer draws on several tools at once: a named or collective subject with the right verb number, a *miután*/*mielőtt* clause for cause and effect, and often a date or a nod to why it still matters today. Practice building sentences like these — this is the kind of answer to practise for a citizenship interview.
